nodes.name: Approval Webhook
nodes.notes:
Header auth, the same token as every other endpoint, so the manager approves with
the curl command included in the alert email.

The honest trade-off: this is not a link you can click from a phone. The two
production answers are a Slack interactive button or a signed magic link with a
secret in lp_config, and neither is here because both add a credential or a
secret that a reviewer cloning this repo would have to create before anything
works. Named in the design doc under production hardening.

nodes.name: Respond Event
nodes.notes:
A duplicate booking answers 200 with duplicate:true, not an error. A provider that
gets an error back re-delivers, and re-delivering something already handled
correctly is how a retry storm starts.

nodes.name: Applies?
nodes.notes:
One gate in front of every side effect, so a 404, a 400 or a duplicate answers the
caller and then stops. Without it each of the six writes below would have to carry
its own guard, and the first one someone forgot would try to upsert an undefined
lead row.

nodes.name: Claim Event
nodes.notes:
Written as `done` in one step rather than claimed-then-completed. An event is a
fact that already happened somewhere else - there is no half-applied state to
recover, unlike a CRM write which can succeed on their side and fail on ours.

nodes.name: Note On Odoo
nodes.notes:
Posted after the field write, so a salesperson opening the record sees the change
and the reason for it side by side. Not waited on - a missing note must never fail
an event that already happened.

nodes.notes:
EDGE CASE 12, the approve half. The verdict is rebuilt from the stored lead and
sent back through the SAME routing workflow, which is already idempotent: it finds
the existing opportunity by external key, moves it from Awaiting Approval to
Qualified, assigns an owner, schedules the cadence and sends the confirmation that
was withheld while the decision was pending.

Enrichment and the AI are deliberately not re-run. Nothing about the lead changed;
only the permission to act on it did, and paying a vendor and a model again to
learn the same thing is waste.

parameters.content:
## LP-06 Events and Approvals

`POST /webhook/lp-event` - `reply | opt_out | booking | close | sales_action`
`POST /webhook/lp-approval` - `{"lead_uid":"...","decision":"approve|reject"}`

**One effect table**, not a branch per event. Each event says what stage it moves to, what it cancels, and whether it closes the opportunity - in one readable object.

**A booking is claimed by its provider id**, so a webhook delivered twice books once, and the second delivery gets a 200 with `duplicate:true` rather than an error that would make the provider retry. **(EC-11)**

**Approve does not reimplement routing** - it flips the state and hands the lead back to LP-03, which is idempotent and already knows how to move, assign, schedule and confirm. **Reject stops all outbound and closes the opportunity as lost. (EC-12)**

**A sales action cancels only the SLA clock**; a reply cancels everything. **(EC-10)**
